page: Hetzner Cloud cpx22 is an x86_64 architecture virtual server powered by the QEMU hypervisor. It features 2 shared vCPUs from the AMD EPYC processor family running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. The server includes 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. There are no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3059.18 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1974.0, both placing in the top 25 percent. However, multi-core and memory performance show limitations. The Geekbench multi-core score of 3532.0 and Passmark CPU score of 5361.29 fall into the bottom 25 percent, reflecting the shared nature of the vCPUs. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average at 70.65 GB/sec for read and 57.5 GB/sec for write, but small block cached read bandwidth is weak. Static web serving throughput is poor, registering at 2.41 GB/sec.

The cpx22 offers a cost-effective entry point for workloads that require moderate single-threaded processing but do not demand sustained multi-core performance or high memory throughput. The shared CPU allocation introduces potential resource contention, making it less suitable for intensive database operations or heavy compilation tasks. It is best suited for lightweight applications, development environments, basic text processing, and small-scale LLM inference using compact models.
